title: operator claim fencing: KMS region attestation + audit-ttl enforcement + RBACv2 service-boundary enforcer
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Added RBACv2 service-boundary enforcer, KMS region attestation helper, and configurable audit TTL enforcement. Backwards compatible; opt-in policy templates provided for Controlled and Sovereign tiers.
description:
Motivation: Customers operating in regulated jurisdictions asked for stricter guarantees that operator/service-account claims cannot cause cross-region key usage and that audit retention windows are enforced by the control plane. This PR implements three coordinated pieces: 1) a RBACv2 'service-boundary' enforcer that constrains operator claims to declared service and zone boundaries; 2) a KMS Region Attestor which validates CMK metadata and rejects key operations when region/zone mismatches are detected; and 3) an audit-ttl enforcement that applies retention policies at ingestion time and exposes a configurable Helm flag for Private installs.

Summary of changes (single-line checklist): 
- [x] RBACv2 enforcer implementation (service boundary rules + policy evaluation cache)
- [x] KMS attestation library and runtime hook (region/owner verification + soft-fallback mode)
- [x] Audit TTL config + configmap template for helm + enforcement path in audit ingester
- [x] Unit + integration tests for core paths and regression for legacy operator flows
- [x] Documentation and migration guide for operators and Private installers

Commits (high-level): 
- feat(authz): add service-boundary enforcer and evaluation cache (3 commits)
- feat(kms): introduce region attestor and wire attestation middleware (2 commits)
- feat(audit): enforce audit TTL at ingestion and add helm config (2 commits)
- test: add enforcer/kms/audit unit tests and integration scenario (4 commits)
- docs: compliance runbook + migration notes (1 commit)

Files / areas touched (high-level): 
- src/authz/enforcer/service_boundary.go (core enforcer + cache)
- src/authz/policies/templates/service-boundary.yaml (policy templates for RBACv2)
- src/kms/attestor/region_validator.go (CMK metadata verification)
- src/kms/hooks/attest_middleware.go (runtime hook used by key-ops path)
- src/audit/ingest/ttl_enforcer.go (applies retention on ingest path)

- examples/helm/values-controlled.yaml (opt-in policy examples for Controlled tier)

Design notes and constraints: 
- Service-boundary policies are expressed as RBACv2 rule templates referencing service:id and zone:region labels. The enforcer consults the operator claim set and denies evaluation if the claim's asserted zone does not match the target resource zone. This is intentionally conservative to avoid silent cross-region key usage.
- KMS attestation validates a configured CMK descriptor (region, account, key-alias) at request start. Two modes are supported: strict (reject on mismatch) and soft-fallback (log + tag request for audit). Default is strict for Dedicated/Private installs and soft-fallback for Hosted while flag rolled out.
- Audit TTL enforcement runs at ingestion to prevent long-retention misconfigurations. Private helm flag makes this opt-in during upgrade windows; Hosted will apply policy centrally.

Review conversation (condensed into single string): 
- Rajiv Patel (review): "High-level LGTM; two concerns: (1) evaluation cache TTL could mask policy updates—add metrics and an admin flush endpoint; (2) need clearer guidance for migrating existing policies to service-boundary templates."
- Maya Chen (author): "Addressed both: added metrics/enforcer.cache.hits|misses and admin API /admin/enforcer/flush; expanded docs with migration steps and a small script to translate common allow rules into service-boundary templates."
- Evelyn Park (security review): "KMS attestor looks good; ensure we fail closed in strict mode and add a circuit breaker to avoid amplifying KMS latency into request latencies."
- Maya Chen: "Added a per-tenant attestor circuit-breaker with a short TTL and fallback tagging behavior; added tests covering circuit open/close."
- Noah Williams (sre): "Audit ingest change needs a rolling upgrade plan for large clusters to avoid spike in GC and indexing. Add a metrics dashboard query for pending retention backlog."
- Maya Chen: "Added PromQL snippets in docs and a low-impact migration note recommending a 24-hour ramp window and retention backfill tooling reference."

CI and validation: 
- CI run 1: build (pass), unit (pass), integration (1 flake in kms_attest_test) — flaky test rerun required.
- CI run 2 (after test fix): build (pass), unit (pass), integration (pass), lint (pass), e2e-smoke (pass). Final status: pass.

Backward compatibility: 
- The enforcer is behind a feature flag (authz.enable_service_boundary) and defaulted to off for existing clusters. Helm values and JSON config examples included. KMS attestor mode defaults to soft-fallback for Hosted; Strict for Dedicated/Private as part of deployment policy. Audit TTL default is disabled on upgrade unless explicitly set.

Security & compliance impact: 
- Improves assurance that operator/service claims cannot cause out-of-zone KMS usage.
- Provides auditable tagging when soft-fallback is used, enabling post-hoc investigations.
- Enforces audit retention at ingester to reduce risk of unbounded retention for regulated tenants.

Migration / rollout notes: 
1) Deploy to staging with authz.enable_service_boundary=true in permissive (soft-fallback) mode for 48h.
2) Validate metrics and check for enforcer denies against legitimate operator flows. Use /admin/enforcer/flush if you need immediate policy changes.
3) For Private installs: set helm private.audit.ttl_days and choose strict attestor mode as desired.
4) For Hosted: centralized rollout will be coordinated with product compliance windows.
